\section[a escola secundária]{a escola secundária — the secondary school}

\label{lesson:PT-C375-escola-secundaria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for available, then the Portuguese for the commitment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a escola secundária}
\textbf{a escola secundária} — \textquotedblleft{}the secondary school\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A minha irmã anda na escola secundária.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My sister goes to secondary school.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal, years 10 to 12; in speech \emph{a secundária}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{escola} is inherited from Latin \emph{schola} \textquotedblleft{}leisure given to learning, a school\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from Greek \emph{skhol\'{\={e}}}, and \emph{secundária} comes from Latin \emph{secundārius} \textquotedblleft{}of the second rank\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{secundus} \textquotedblleft{}following\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a escola secundária}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a escola secundária}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a escola secundária}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for available, then the Portuguese for the commitment, then say \emph{a escola secundária} again
\end{itemize}

\section[frequentar]{frequentar — to attend; to go to often}

\label{lesson:PT-C375-frequentar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the commitment, then the Portuguese for the secondary school.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: frequentar}
\textbf{frequentar} — \textquotedblleft{}to attend; to go to often\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele frequenta aulas de inglês à noite.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He attends English classes in the evening.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Frequentar um curso} — to attend a course.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{frequentar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{frequentāre} \textquotedblleft{}to visit or resort to frequently\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), on \emph{frequēns} \textquotedblleft{}crowded, frequent\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[a falta]{a falta — the absence (from class); the lack; the foul}

\label{lesson:PT-C375-falta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the secondary school, then the Portuguese for to attend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a falta}
\textbf{a falta} — \textquotedblleft{}the absence (from class); the lack; the foul\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tive uma falta porque cheguei atrasado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I was marked absent because I arrived late.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer falta} — to be missed or needed; \emph{sem falta} — without fail. In football, a foul.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{falta} is built on \emph{faltar} \textquotedblleft{}to be missing\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Vulgar Latin \emph{fallita}, from Latin \emph{fallere} \textquotedblleft{}to deceive, to disappoint\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a pauta]{a pauta — the list of marks; the musical stave}

\label{lesson:PT-C375-pauta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to attend, then the Portuguese for the absence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a pauta}
\textbf{a pauta} — \textquotedblleft{}the list of marks; the musical stave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
As notas já estão na pauta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The marks are already on the list.}
\end{quote}

A European school word: the posted list of final marks. Also a stave in music.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pauta} goes back to Latin \emph{pacta} \textquotedblleft{}agreements\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), the plural of \emph{pactum} \textquotedblleft{}an agreement\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): first a written list of terms, then any ruled list.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a disciplina]{a disciplina — the school subject; discipline}

\label{lesson:PT-C375-disciplina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the absence, then the Portuguese for the list of marks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a disciplina}
\textbf{a disciplina} — \textquotedblleft{}the school subject; discipline\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A minha disciplina preferida é a história.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My favourite subject is history.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal \emph{uma disciplina} is a school subject; also discipline, order.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disciplina} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{disciplīna} \textquotedblleft{}instruction, teaching\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{discipulus} \textquotedblleft{}pupil\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{discere} \textquotedblleft{}to learn\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
